title: NBF Grade XI Unit7 Comprehensive Questions 7.1–7.8: first-pass physics and FBISE review, teacher HOLD
evidenceBoundary: Eight question numbers/prompts cross-checked between a prior private student-practice edition, a prior solved draft, and a public chapter transcription; original scanned page pixels not available for fresh image-bound audit. Prior book SHA is provenance carried forward, NOT recomputed. Derivative explanations are candidates requiring independent teacher approval.

items.academicConcern: Distinguish single-crystal order, many oriented crystalline grains, and absence of long-range periodicity in amorphous solids; avoid implying polycrystalline solids are noncrystalline.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; teacher response should explicitly distinguish single crystals from polycrystalline aggregates and label polymer classification a different axis.

items.academicConcern: A unit cell tiles the lattice by translation; the common SC/BCC/FCC cells are conventional cubic descriptions, but BCC/FCC conventional cells are not the primitive cells. The seven crystal systems categorize geometry, not the three cubic centering arrangements.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; distinguish primitive/conventional cells, SC/BCC/FCC, lattice points versus atoms in a basis, and seven geometric crystal systems; no misleading smallest-cell rule.

items.academicConcern: Stress/strain are mode-dependent pairs; modulus as a constant stress-to-strain ratio presumes the appropriate proportional/linear elastic regime. A definition-only question is Understanding, not automatically B-24 Application.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; give units and matching strain type, state the linear-regime assumption, and use separate applied questions if direct B-24 Application evidence is needed.

items.academicConcern: A ductile tensile curve is typically engineering stress vertically versus engineering strain horizontally; yield plateau and upper/lower yield points are material-dependent. Proportional limit, elastic limit, ultimate engineering stress and fracture must not be conflated.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; require a clearly labelled qualitative curve and correct region definitions; no inference of universal point letters or a specific steel-only plateau.

items.academicConcern: Elastic recovery can occur beyond strict linear proportionality before the elastic limit; plastic deformation creates residual strain, but does not necessarily imply fracture. Unloading path is distinct from initial loading.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; explain unloading and permanent set on a labelled stress-strain diagram, separating the elastic limit from the proportional limit.

items.academicConcern: Physical work is integral of force with respect to extension, not graph slope or a generic shaded area with reversed axes. NBF Fig.7.14 prints extension vertically and weight horizontally; the standard under-curve area argument needs force vertical and extension horizontal, especially for nonlinear behavior.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; explicitly define F vertical and x horizontal, derive W=integral(F dx), and restrict W=Fx/2 to straight-line zero-start Hooke behavior.

items.academicConcern: U=Fx/2=kx^2/2=YA(DeltaL)^2/(2L) presumes quasistatic loading from zero in the linear elastic range. A stress-strain integral is energy per unit volume, not automatically the total joules stored; plastic hysteresis changes recoverability.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; show force-extension assumptions, distinguish joules from J/m3, and label any energy-density derivation supplementary.

items.academicConcern: A wire Young-modulus measurement needs original effective gauge length, diameter-based area, applied force change and corresponding extension; force-extension measurements should share a consistent initial reading and remain within the elastic range. Optional reference wire is not compulsory from the source figure.
items.reviewAction: Retain the original; require a source-faithful apparatus description, F=mg with consistent load baseline, Y=FL/(A DeltaL), labels, SI units, and measurement precautions without misattributing enrichment to Fig7.13.
